newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Asian crude weakens, but differentials steady.
newsitem.headline: Asian crude weakens, but differentials steady.

text.p: Asian crude prices were lower on Tuesday as a supply overhang continued to depress the market.
But differentials were mostly steady while buyers and sellers stayed at a stand off.
The Minas market was talked at ICP -30/-20 to ICP flat. The last done remained ICP -15/20.
Middle East trading was also quiet with most buyers relaxed and not chasing any deals. A Thai refinery was heard taking a cargo of Oman at MPM -4 cents, in line with the market.
A European major denied selling Umm Shaif at ADNOC +12 cents, two cents below a deal last week.
The weaker tone of the cash Brent market was reflected in a narrowing of the Brent/Dubai spread.
May was quoted at $1.35/$1.45, in from $1.45/$1.55 in New York late on Monday.
Traders said that would leave the arbitrage for West African crudes open, although a high level of turnarounds was leaving buyers relaxed.
April Tapis swaps were down 35 cents on the day at $21.10/$21.15. A Wall Streeter sold April Tapis swaps at $21.15.
A Tapis producer targetted plus $1.00 for cash Tapis, but most traders said the market was more like +60/70 cents.
They said many buyers would wait for the result of the Bangchak refinery tender and the Indian Oil Corp tender, which are scheduled to be awarded Friday, for the next price direction.
